lead: Try the sketch before opening an answer. These questions belong to its quarter-gap arithmetic, not to a measured swimming cell.

rows.title: Does moving the input also move the background?
rows.question: Reset the sketch, then set its input to four without using One update. Which readout changes, and which stays at zero?
rows.answer: The current input becomes four and the response becomes four. The background stays at zero until One update closes a quarter of the gap. Changing a condition is not the same action as adapting to it.

rows.title: Can a positive input have a negative response?
rows.question: From zero background, set the input to four and use One update twice. Then lower the input to one without updating again. Is the response still positive?
rows.answer: The two updates made the background one, then one-and-three-quarters. Lowering the input to one leaves that background in place, so the response is minus three-quarters. Positive input does not guarantee a positive difference.

rows.title: Does waiting one second count as an update?
rows.question: Raise an input, leave the sketch alone for a moment, and compare its update count. Did time spent reading reduce its gap?
rows.answer: No. This sketch changes its background only when you request an update. One update is not one biological second, and waiting does not secretly add samples. The arithmetic shows a relationship without supplying a real adaptation rate.
